Marissa / Lauren — sketching the technical approach below; feel free to lift into contract wording.

1) Measurement definitions
- Per-request latency measured from ingress to final token emission finish (inclusive of routing).
- p50/p95 computed on request-level latencies. For operational monitoring we maintain rolling 1-hour percentiles (sliding window updated every minute).
- For contractual SLA month-level computation, we use calendar-day buckets aggregated into the monthly SLA. Each calendar day’s p95 comes from 5-minute sampling of the rolling 1-hour metric and we take the daily p95. Monthly p95 is the weighted median of daily p95s (weights = request counts per day).

2) Exception / carveout handling during launch
- Temporary carveout window: 14 calendar days from production cutover. During that window, p95 SLO will be evaluated with a burst-tolerant threshold: allow up to 2x forecasted p95 for periods where request rate > 150% of baseline for > 10 minutes. Any carveout applied must be accompanied by:
  a. evidence snapshot (request-rate graphs, rolling 1-hour p95 traces)
  b. incident notes explaining traffic source and mitigation plan
  c. joint sign-off from both engineering leads (Helios + Redwood)

3) Credit calculation
- Credits apply if monthly p95 exceeds committed threshold for more than 3 calendar days in the month after accounting for approved carveouts. Credits are prorated to usage on days exceeding the bound.

Open items for legal to frame: exact wording for weighted aggregation and the signature mechanism for carveout sign-off (DocuSign link for formal approval).

Ethan — looping in contractual language below and a proposed operational playbook for the 14-day carveout. I’ve also uploaded a draft amendment for signature (redwood_docusign-hosted-slo-amendment.pdf).

Proposed contract paragraph (draft):
"During an initial Production Ramp period (the \"Ramp Period\") of up to fourteen (14) consecutive calendar days following Customer's first production cutover to Redwood's Hosted API, the parties agree that any exceedance of the p95 latency commitment shall be evaluated for eligibility for a Ramp Period Relief. Relief may be granted if (i) the exceedance coincides with sustained traffic above 150% of the Customer's agreed baseline for longer than ten (10) minutes, (ii) Customer provides a contemporaneous evidence package comprised of request-rate metrics and rolling percentile traces, and (iii) both parties sign the Ramp Period Relief Form. Any Relief approved shall be time-boxed to the Ramp Period and explicitly excluded from the monthly SLA credit calculation."

Operational playbook:
- Day 0 (cutover): enable verbose tracing and a pinned dashboard shared via Ops link.
- Day 1–14: automated anomaly detection alerts to both parties for p95 > 1.5x baseline.
- Evidence package: daily export of rolling 1-hour p95 series + request-rate heatmap.
- Decision: Relief request submitted via email + Ops ticket; Redwood has 12 hours to acknowledge and 48 hours to review, after which both parties sign DocuSign.

I recommend we add the DocuSign amendment as an appendix to the main order form (I attached the draft link). If that works, Marissa — please share with Procurement and Legal. Ethan — once you confirm, I’ll send the DocuSign envelope and include the Ramp Period Relief Form template for you to sign.

Regards,
